[Here](http://triblive.com/news/adminpage/10228748-74/wtae-bell-post) is a link to the story. Basically, there was a shooting in Wilkinsburg, just east of the city, and 5 adults and an unborn child were killed. She made some comments about the suspects even though next to nothing is known about the shooters, and then made a comment about a young black man working at a restaurant busing tables, basically saying "he is one of the good ones" (paraphrase).

You can read the Facebook post for yourself, a copy of it (it has since been taken down and Bell has apologized) is in the link I posted, but I'd like to have a bit of a discussion about it here. I personally don't think either side was 100% in the right. Obviously the post stereotyped in a pretty negative way, although in my opinion, I don't think Bell was trying to be offensive. She is well known throughout the community and pretty well liked, and based the last paragraph and her mentioning hope, I truly believe it was meant to be inspirational and not offensive.

That being said, I can see how this would obviously offend people, and posting it was definitely a lapse in judgement. However, I don't think firing her is appropriate. It ends the discussion on race right then and there. "Oh, you said something racist, well we're not gonna talk about it just leave." That doesn't help anything. I think it would've been more helpful to possibly give her a suspension and time to think about what she said. Then when she returns to work, or maybe even before returning, interview her about what she learned. Get members of the community involved; have white kids asking questions that confuse them about race; have black kids offer insight into marginalized culture. Basically, *HAVE AN OPEN DISCUSSION*. I think Wendy Bell's localized fame is a perfect opportunity to host these kinds of discussions, but once again, American mainstream media has swept the issue under the rug, and another opportunity to grow as a culture has been lost in the name of TV ratings.
Stories like this come out all the time, but Pittsburgh news anchor Wendy Bell has been fired for a racially insensitive Facebook post.

What you ask for is reasonable. But the problem is that when you're the face of a company and you say something un-PC, the company takes the hit. If they don't respond as they do, the entire company suffers. It's the same as the Alison Rapp thing. Nintendo isn't going to have a PR person being a camwhore on the side. It affects their public image, which in their case is a family friendly co. And a news org is 'supposed' to be impartial, so a racist post isn't that. So while what you ask for is reasonable, they feel the need to take immediate action and look good. In short if you're the very public face of a company, use your brain before you open your mouth.
